messages:
sara: Heads-up — we're launching the lightweight-adapters plugin for the JS/Py SDKs and the docs are live in internal preview: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/lightweight-adapters. This is an opt-in feature that makes it easier to swap small routing/transform logic into the client without running a full adapter service. Rollout plan: canary on hosted API tomorrow 09:00 PDT, gradual rollout to all customers over 2 weeks. Migration notes below.
matt: Nice! any breaking changes we should worry about? :eyes:
sara: Minimal. The public API changes are small but intentional: `register_adapter()` is renamed to `registerConnector()` to make naming consistent across languages. Old name is shimmed for one release but will be removed after the 2-week rollout. So plan: bump minor, but test for lints and CI. Example (JS):
```js
// old
client.register_adapter('my-adapter', opts)
// new
client.registerConnector('my-adapter', { transform: opts })
```
jessica: Ok — will the examples in the examples repo be updated automatically or do we need a PR?
sara: We'll push automated codemods for the common patterns today and open PRs to the examples repo. We still need owners to review and approve. Assigning @lia to own the examples PRs and coordinate with SDK reviewers. :point_right:
lia: On it — I'll watch for the codemod output and queue the PRs. ETA EOD today.
matt: Telemetry question — does this new plugin send any usage data by default? We need to be sure it's OK for dedicated/private customers.
sara: Good call. Telemetry is opt-in by default for lightweight-adapters. There is a single flag: `enableAdapterTelemetry: true|false`. For Private/Dedicated the default is false. For Hosted trial users we default false until they explicitly enable it. We'll document the fields and the minimal telemetry schema (start/stop, error code, no payloads). Short sample (py):
```py
client.registerConnector('my-adapter', transform=my_fn, enableAdapterTelemetry=False)
```
matt: Perfect.
jessica: Anything for SDK maintainers re: test coverage or lint? We should gate merges on integration tests.
sara: Yes — required CI checks: unit coverage >= 90% for the adapter module, integration tests against the canary endpoint, and docs linter green. I'm adding a release checklist in the PR template.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: docs/lightweight-adapters -> preview cluster at 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z (canary).
sara: Please review the internal doc and samples: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/sdk/lightweight-adapters-preview. If you see anything risky (security, telemetry, or breaking behavior) call it out here. Otherwise we'll proceed with the canary tomorrow. :party:
